questions.question: Who were the parents of William H. Ferber (b. December 1869, Ohio; d. 11 March 1903, Cincinnati, Hamilton, Ohio)?
questions.rationale: The research objective directly targets William's parental origins. Identifying his parents is the gatekeeper question prerequisite to tracing geographic origins. Born December 1869 in Ohio and resident in Cincinnati his entire recorded life, William would appear in his parents' household in the 1870 and 1880 U.S. censuses. His 1903 Ohio death certificate and 1890 Hamilton County marriage record are primary documents that may name his parents directly. Hamilton County probate and church records are secondary candidates.

items.rationale: William was born December 1869 and would appear as an infant in his parents' household in the June 1870 census. The household head (his father) and wife (his mother) would be named, along with any siblings. This is the highest-probability source for direct parentage evidence.

William would be approximately 10 years old in June 1880 and almost certainly still living with his parents. The census names both parents and all household members, corroborating the 1870 finding and adding birthplace data for the parents.

William died 11 March 1903 in Cincinnati. Ohio death records from this era name the decedent's parents when the informant knew them. His wife Emma, as the likely informant, would have known his parents' names. The FamilySearch collection 'Ohio, County Death Records, 1840-2001' covers Hamilton County.

The marriage record for William H. Ferber and Emma Becker (10 Sep 1890, Hamilton County) is already sourced (SLJ6-N3L). The original image must be examined: Ohio marriage registers and bonds sometimes name the groom's father or require parental consent. The index entry alone may not capture parental data.

Cincinnati had a large German immigrant community and well-documented German Lutheran and Catholic churches. A baptism record for William circa December 1869 would name both parents and the mother's maiden name. FamilySearch holds microfilmed Cincinnati church records for this period.

William's parents would appear in the 1860 census before his birth. Once their names are known from the 1870/1880 census, searching 1860 confirms their prior location and gives the father's occupation, property, and state of birth — evidence that may point to the family's geographic origin.

After identifying William's parents from the census, searching for their marriage record directly addresses the second part of the objective (geographic origins) by naming the mother's maiden name and possibly giving a place of origin. Ohio County Marriages 1789-2016 on FamilySearch covers Hamilton and adjacent counties.

Fallback for pli_003. Ancestry's 'Ohio, U.S., Death Records, 1908-1932' and city death registers may hold the 1903 Cincinnati death certificate for William H. Ferber if FamilySearch coverage is incomplete for pre-1908 Hamilton County.

FamilySearch public member trees may document the Ferber family in Cincinnati and provide leads to additional sources. Treat as a compiled/derivative source only — any parentage found here requires verification against original records before use as evidence.
